methodology.note: Autocomplete is used only as a directional intent proxy. It does not provide monthly search volume or ranking difficulty.
methodology.observedVsInferred: Every signal lists observed evidence separately from AVIORA interpretation.

observed: China Highlights states that 80% of first-time visitors choose its core 1-2 week plans.
China Highlights, Wendy Wu, Original Travel, Scott Dunn and AVIORA all maintain Beijing-Xi'an-Shanghai variants.
categorySignals.inferred: This is the largest mature demand pool, but route-level differentiation is weak.

observed: WildChina, China Highlights, Wendy Wu and Jacada all sell panda-led or family-led China products.
Wendy Wu displays 86 reviews on In Pursuit of Pandas.
categorySignals.inferred: Pandas are one of the strongest emotional entry points for families and multigenerational groups.

observed: WildChina publishes a dedicated Chongqing editorial journey.
China Highlights publishes an 18-day New China product and an 8-day Chengdu-Jiuzhaigou-Chongqing product.
Wendy Wu sells New Horizons of China around Chongqing and Zhangjiajie.
categorySignals.inferred: The category is moving from social-media inspiration into bookable products but remains less saturated than the classic triangle.

observed: Intrepid operates a dedicated 10-day China Real Food Adventure with displayed reviews and pricing.
Food experiences are also prominent inside WildChina, Scott Dunn and family itineraries.
categorySignals.inferred: A private premium culinary journey is validated but under-supplied compared with generic sightseeing products.

observed: China Highlights maintains a priced 12-day Xi'an-Kashgar private product.
Google Autocomplete returns package, itinerary, senior and Australia variants for 'china silk road tour'.
categorySignals.inferred: Long-tail intent is clear and ticket value is high, but operational complexity makes this a second-wave product.
